UNICEF's 2024/25 national budget brief describes how conflict damage to schools and hospitals creates a need for more spending on reconstruction. With the finance and health ministers among those training at Hurso, their portfolios suggest practical tests of preparedness. How would the government protect funding for essential services? How would it keep hospitals supplied and ambulances running in areas affected by fighting? What diplomatic channels remain open? Public accountability for decisions on force The exercises and the diplomatic dispute warrant scrutiny together. Abiy's account explains the purpose he assigned to the training. The correspondence reported by Reuters records competing claims about the border and the threat of force. A public case for any military action would require evidence about what happened, a lawful justification for the proposed response, and an explanation of how the government intends to protect civilians. Those are the standards by which Ethiopians should be able to judge their leaders' decisions. This event occurred shortly after Ethiopia severed diplomatic ties with Eritrea, raising questions about the implications of military readiness in the context of escalating tensions. Abiy framed the training as a leadership development initiative, emphasizing the importance of civilian officials understanding military operations for better coordination during crises. However, the timing of the exercises may also signal a potential acceptance of military confrontation with Eritrea. As Ethiopia faces significant humanitarian challenges, including a collapsing health system in northern regions, the government's military preparedness and its impact on public services and accountability remain critical issues for citizens to evaluate.

ethiopia.title: News - 'People Are Getting Desperate': Jimma Protests Expose Growing Anger Over Forced Conscription, Extortion
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: News - 'People Are Getting Desperate': Jimma Protests Expose Growing Anger Over Forced Conscription, Extortion - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: News - 'People Are Getting Desperate': Jimma Protests Expose Growing Anger Over Forced Conscription, Extortion 12 November 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — Residents of Jimma city in southwestern Oromia zone in Ethiopia say protests that erupted on Monday and Tuesday were driven by mounting grievances over widespread forced conscription, arbitrary arrests, extortion and displacement, describing an increasingly desperate population with few avenues to seek redress from authorities. The demonstrations, which were particularly intense in the Bore neighborhood of Jimma city, were triggered by the killing of a former Ethiopian National Defense Force (ENDF) member who had reportedly sustained injuries while serving in the military. However, residents interviewed by Addis Standard said the incident was only the immediate trigger for broader discontent over deteriorating security and administrative malpractices. "The conscription is not the only reason," said Kediro Abbabulgu, a resident of Kes Sefer in Jimma. "Although the killing of the former ENDF member triggered the protests, the people are also protesting against the mistreatment of civilians by the police and local militia." Kediro said residents were facing multiple forms of economic and administrative pressure, including what he described as "excessive and unexplained taxation, arbitrary demands for proof of purchase receipts" and alleged extortion by security personnel. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn He said police officers and local militia were increasingly stopping people leaving markets and shopping areas and demanding receipts for their purchases. Those unable to produce them were allegedly beaten, detained or pressured to pay bribes to secure their release. "The people of Jimma are silently being exploited," he said, adding that residents who attempted to raise concerns with local authorities were often confronted with claims that the city was becoming a "leading example of prosperity". Kediro also cited what he described as widespread evictions linked to urban corridor development projects, alleging that affected residents were being displaced without adequate compensation. A second resident, who spoke to Addis Standard on condition of anonymity for fear of reprisals, described a growing sense of powerlessness among residents, saying they no longer knew where to turn when confronted with administrative abuses. "We don't know who is governing us," the resident said. "If you go to any government office to file a complaint over administrative wrongdoings, they will tell you the direction came from the federal government and that they have no authority to solve the problem. Even corruption complaints are referred to the federal government." The resident said the situation had become increasingly alarming over the past month, alleging that young men were being forcibly taken from streets, homes, workplaces and even places of worship, with families often left without information about their whereabouts. "Young men are disappearing and no one knows where they are being taken," the resident said. "The people of Jimma are getting desperate." According to the resident, the protests were not organized by any identifiable group but emerged from accumulated public frustration. The resident further alleged that security forces had since been pressuring residents to identify individuals they considered organizers of the demonstrations. The same source said security forces were also arresting parents, accusing them of sending their children to join the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA), an armed group fighting the federal government in Oromia. "More than 50 people are detained on Wednesday," the resident said, adding that residents had also reported at least three people killed by security forces during Tuesday's confrontations. Addis Standard could not independently verify the reported death toll or the number of arrests. The accounts from Jimma come against a broader backdrop of recurring allegations of forced conscription, arbitrary detention and extortion across Oromia, documented by Addis Standard and the Ethiopian Human Rights Commission (EHRC). In a report published in late 2024, the EHRC documented allegations of unlawful forced recruitment, arbitrary detentions and extortion in several Oromia towns, including Jimma, Adama, Bishoftu and Shashemane. The commission's findings included cases involving children as young as 11 . More recently, Addis Standard reporting has documented renewed allegations of forced conscription in parts of Oromia, including Sheger City, East Hararghe and East Bale, with families reporting that young men were taken against their will and, in some instances, subsequent demands for money to secure their release. Other reporting has highlighted pressure on rural communities to participate in regional militia and security training programs, with allegations that access to essential agricultural services and supplies has sometimes been used as leverage. The region's security administration also o perates through multiple layers of formal and parallel structures , including regional, zonal and district peace and security offices and security councils. The institutionalization of the Gaachana Sirnaa (Shield of the System) security structure under Oromia Proclamation No. 245/2022 has for years drawn scrutiny from critics who say the expanding security apparatus has contributed to coercion and a climate of impunity. Oromia regional authorities have previously rejected allegations of widespread forced conscription and abductions for ransom, dismissing some accounts as propaganda intended to undermine the region's security institutions. ethiopia.summary: Protests erupted in Jimma city, Ethiopia, driven by widespread grievances over forced conscription, arbitrary arrests, extortion, and displacement. The demonstrations, particularly intense in the Bore neighborhood, were sparked by the killing of a former Ethiopian National Defense Force member but reflect deeper discontent regarding deteriorating security and administrative abuses. Residents report excessive taxation, demands for purchase receipts, and mistreatment by police and local militia, leading to a growing sense of desperation. Many young men have reportedly disappeared after being forcibly taken by security forces, leaving families in distress. The protests emerged from accumulated frustration rather than being organized by any specific group. Security forces have responded with arrests and pressure on residents to identify protest organizers. Allegations of forced conscription and extortion have been documented across Oromia, with regional authorities denying these claims and labeling them as propaganda. The situation highlights a climate of impunity and increasing unrest among the population. (158 words)

ethiopia.title: Ethiopia Faces Contrasting Drought, Flood Risks As Potentially Record-Strength Super El Niño Looms
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia Faces Contrasting Drought, Flood Risks As Potentially Record-Strength Super El Niño Looms - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia Faces Contrasting Drought, Flood Risks As Potentially Record-Strength Super El Niño Looms 12 November 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — Ethiopia could face contrasting climate risks, with parts of the country exposed to worsening drought while southern areas brace for above-normal rainfall and potential flooding, as a potentially record-strength Super El Niño develops in 2026-27, according to an analysis by international water and sanitation organization WaterAid. The analysis, b ased on 44 years of rainfall data spanning 1982 to 2025 and previous El Niño events, identifies Ethiopia as an exception to the broader East African rainfall pattern, with stronger El Niño conditions generally associated with drier conditions in parts of the country, including Addis Abeba. WaterAid said the effects of El Niño are not uniform across Ethiopia, highlighting an east-west divide that could expose different parts of the country to distinct climate-related threats. Addis Abeba, for instance, experienced one of its driest periods on record during the 2015-16 El Niño event. The analysis warns that worsening dryness in northern and central Ethiopia could place additional pressure on reservoirs, municipal water supplies and agricultural production, potentially compounding existing water-security challenges. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn In contrast, southern Ethiopia is expected to experience above-normal rainfall during the October-December short rainy season. Regional forecasts cited in the analysis indicate an approximately 90% likelihood of wetter-than-normal conditions across parts of Kenya, Somalia and southern Ethiopia, raising concerns over flooding and damage to infrastructure. The opposing rainfall patterns could intensify pressure on water and sanitation systems, with drought threatening water availability in some areas while heavy rainfall risks damaging infrastructure, contaminating water supplies and increasing exposure to waterborne diseases, including cholera. WaterAid's assessment also identifies Ethiopia's coffee-growing regions as potentially exposed to wider supply-chain disruptions associated with climate extremes. Across the wider Horn of Africa, the analysis points to a stronger likelihood of wetter conditions in Kenya, particularly Nairobi, Somalia, Tanzania, including Dar es Salaam, and Uganda, including Kampala. These areas could face heightened risks of heavy rainfall, flash floods, infrastructure damage and outbreaks of waterborne diseases. The projected conditions contrast with the broader drought signal across southern Africa, where parts of South Africa, Botswana, Zimbabwe and southern Mozambique are particularly exposed to below-normal rainfall. In West Africa, the drying signal is concentrated mainly along the coastal belt rather than the Sahel. WaterAid said its assessment draws on the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), using Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Station data (CHIRPS), correlated with the strength of the Niño 3.4 climate indicator. The analysis examines rainfall patterns across 20 cities in three African regions. While historical El Niño events provide an indication of where climate impacts are likely to occur, WaterAid cautioned that previous patterns may underestimate the potential severity of the current event given its projected intensity. It also warned that stronger El Niño conditions could amplify existing regional climate patterns, increasing the likelihood of droughts and floods, disrupting agriculture and livelihoods, and placing additional pressure on already vulnerable communities. These impacts need not translate into humanitarian emergencies if governments and development partners take anticipatory measures, strengthen climate-resilient water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) systems, and invest in water security before extreme conditions materialize. The organization also called for water security to receive greater p riority at the COP31 climate summit, arguing that resilient water and sanitation infrastructure is essential to protecting communities from increasingly severe climate extremes. "The findings point to mounting pressure on water security, urban resilience and economic stability, as millions of people face the threat of increasingly unpredictable and extreme weather as the current 2026-27 Super El Niño event heads towards record strength." An analysis by WaterAid indicates that while northern and central regions may experience worsening drought conditions, southern Ethiopia is expected to see above-normal rainfall, raising the risk of flooding. This contrasting weather pattern highlights an east-west divide in Ethiopia, with Addis Ababa having previously faced severe dryness during past El Niño events. The anticipated drought could strain water supplies and agricultural production, exacerbating existing water-security issues. Conversely, the increased rainfall in the south poses risks of flooding, infrastructure damage, and waterborne diseases. WaterAid emphasizes the need for proactive measures to enhance water security and climate-resilient systems, particularly ahead of the COP31 climate summit. The analysis warns that without intervention, the impacts of these extreme weather patterns could threaten the livelihoods and stability of vulnerable communities across the region. (159 words)

ethiopia.title: Ivorian Former Prime Minister Recognizes Ethiopia's Legitimate Sea Access Aspirations
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: Ivorian Former Prime Minister Recognizes Ethiopia's Legitimate Sea Access Aspirations - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: Ivorian Former Prime Minister Recognizes Ethiopia's Legitimate Sea Access Aspirations 12 November 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — Former Prime Minister of Côte d'Ivoire and President of the Ivorian Popular Front (FPI), Pascal Affi N'Guessan, recognized Ethiopia's quest for sovereign sea access as a legitimate national aspiration. Speaking to ENA in Addis Ababa, Affi N'Guessan said Ethiopia's ambitions deserved recognition, expressing hope that outstanding issues could be addressed through solutions acceptable to all parties. His remarks come at a time when Ethiopia is actively pursuing permanent access to the Red Sea, citing its geographical, historical and economic circumstances. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines The East African nation has repeatedly underscored that its quest for sea access is peaceful, emphasizing that the current status of being geographically landlocked should not remain an enduring constraint on its national development. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has particularly described Ethiopia's pursuit of Red Sea access as an overdue national aspiration. "A population of over 130 million people cannot remain landlocked. A generation of today will not bequeath a geographically imprisoned nation to posterity," he stressed. The country's geographical proximity to the Red Sea, together with its historical links to the region's ports, has remained central to its push for securing a sovereign sea outlet. Ethiopia historically administered the ports of Massawa and Assab and maintained naval capabilities before Eritrea's independence. Pascal Affi N'Guessan, who served as Côte d'Ivoire's prime minister from 2000 to 2003, underscored that Ethiopia's ambition to secure access to a seaport is legitimate. "I believe that the ambition of Ethiopia is legitimate, and we hope that these questions will find solutions acceptable to all parties, through good compromises that allow everyone to recognize that this is the path that enables the entire region to move forward," he said. He emphasized that meaningful compromises and a spirit of cooperation were essential to ensuring that differing interests do not become obstacles to regional progress. His message also highlights the broader significance of African-led solutions, mutual respect and cooperation in building lasting stability and advancing collective prosperity across the continent. Affi N'Guessan further said Ethiopia's quest for sea access should be approached with an understanding of its broader geopolitical implications and the shared future of countries in the Horn of Africa. "Well, these are geopolitical questions very important, which necessitate capacities of dialogue, capacities of dialogue, capacities of anticipation," he said. ethiopia.title: COP32 Ethiopia Crucial Platform for Global South Consensus Beyond Climate Finance
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: COP32 Ethiopia Crucial Platform for Global South Consensus Beyond Climate Finance - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: COP32 Ethiopia Crucial Platform for Global South Consensus Beyond Climate Finance 12 November 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — Ethiopia's hosting of COP32 in 2027 offers Global South nations a vital opportunity to build consensus, coordinate negotiating positions, and broaden climate discussions beyond financing, said Organization of Southern Cooperation (OSC) Secretary-General Manssour Bin Mussallam. Speaking to ENA, Bin Mussallam emphasized that COP32 can reshape global climate negotiations by framing developing countries not merely as victims of climate impacts, but as leading contributors to global climate action, policy innovation, and concrete solutions. "The agenda of COP32 in Ethiopia can change the regular dynamic, where the South is seen only as a victim of the climate crisis. It can instead become a platform where countries of the South come together to articulate proposals and ideas rooted in our own commitments and priorities," he said. According to Bin Mussallam, Ethiopia is strategically positioned to facilitate this process through its role as host of the African Union headquarters and COP32. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines He said the country could provide platforms for Global South nations to build consensus and coordinate their positions before engaging in international climate negotiations, enabling them to advance shared interests more effectively. The OSC Secretary General stressed that cooperation among developing countries should extend beyond climate finance to include strategic coordination among nations producing critical minerals required for renewable energy technologies, including solar panels and electric vehicles. Such cooperation, he explained, would enable resource-producing countries to strengthen their capacity to regulate mineral exports, improve their bargaining positions, and secure greater participation in global clean energy value chains. He further emphasized that the transition to clean energy should be driven by the productive capabilities, resources, and industrial potential of developing countries themselves. In this regard, he called for a shift away from the existing economic model in which developing countries export raw materials while importing finished renewable energy technologies. "We should no longer export raw materials and import solar panels. We should instead produce renewable energy technologies within our own countries, achieving both ecological sustainability and economic prosperity," he emphasized. Bin Mussallam also called on developed countries to complement climate finance commitments with increased investment in industrial development across the Global South. "While climate finance remains important and reflects fair reparations from countries that have contributed most to the climate crisis, our partners in the North should also invest in transforming our critical minerals into renewable energy technologies within our own countries," he said. He noted that such investments could help developing countries accelerate the clean energy transition while creating employment opportunities, strengthening domestic industries, promoting technology transfer, and supporting sustainable economic growth. Ethiopia is preparing to host COP32 in Addis Ababa in 2027, providing an opportunity to connect international climate commitments with the development priorities of Africa and other developing regions. The conference is expected to contribute to broader discussions on aligning climate adaptation, trade policies, industrial development, and development finance with practical and scalable outcomes in areas such as food security and sustainable energy. He highlighted that the conference could redefine the narrative surrounding developing countries, positioning them as proactive contributors to climate solutions rather than just victims of climate change. COP32 aims to align climate adaptation with Africa's development priorities, addressing issues like food security and sustainable energy while fostering economic growth.

ethiopia.title: PM Abiy Urges Major Emitters to Step Up, Intensifies Diplomatic Outreach Ahead of Ethiopia's COP32
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: PM Abiy Urges Major Emitters to Step Up, Intensifies Diplomatic Outreach Ahead of Ethiopia's COP32 - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: PM Abiy Urges Major Emitters to Step Up, Intensifies Diplomatic Outreach Ahead of Ethiopia's COP32 12 November 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed (PhD) has urged major greenhouse gas emitters to accelerate emissions reductions and deliver faster climate financing, as Ethiopia seeks to build international partnerships ahead of hosting the 32nd United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP32) in Addis Abeba next year. Alongside the summit, Abiy held bilateral discussions with the leaders of Somalia, Barbados, Finland, Norway, Qatar, Iraq and Botswana, as well as United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres, seeking to advance bilateral cooperation and strengthen international engagement ahead of Ethiopia's COP32 presidency. Addressing world leaders at the COP31 summit in Antalya, Türkiye, on 11 November, Abiy called on countries with the greatest historical responsibility for greenhouse gas emissions and the financial capacity to act to lead with deeper emissions cuts during the current decade. According to Anadolu Agency , Abiy said the growing cost of responding to climate-related damage was diverting resources from essential development priorities, including education, healthcare and opportunities for young people. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn "The more we spend coping with climate damage, the less we have to invest in schools, health care and opportunity for our young people," he said. Abiy highlighted Ethiopia's efforts to reduce emissions, including its 2024 restrictions on imports of petrol- and diesel-powered vehicles as the country pursues a transition towards electric mobility. He said Ethiopia would prioritize early intervention and faster climate financing when it assumes the COP32 presidency. The prime minister's diplomatic engagements included a meeting with Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, during which the two leaders discussed bilateral relations and regional security, according to the Somali National News Agency ( SONNA ). They reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation and advancing shared prosperity. Abiy also met Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan on 10 November. According to Anadolu Agency, Erdoğan pledged continued cooperation with Ethiopia, particularly in trade and investment, and reaffirmed Türkiye's support for peace and stability in the region. He also congratulated Ethiopia on preparations to host COP32. Other engagements included discussions with Barbados Prime Minister Mia Mottley on aviation cooperation and collaboration supporting Ethiopia's COP32 presidency, while talks with Finnish President Alexander Stubb covered bilateral relations, international developments and climate diplomacy. The diplomatic engagements come as Ethiopia seeks to use its upcoming COP32 presidency to expand international partnerships and secure support for its climate priorities. On 9 November, Addis Standard reported that Foreign Affairs Minister Gedion Timothewos , who is also Ethiopia's COP32 President-Designate, described the country's participation in COP31 as an opportunity to prepare for hosting the next summit. He highlighted planned cooperation with Türkiye and Australia, the establishment of an Ethiopian pavilion and efforts to showcase the country's climate mitigation initiatives. Gedion also emphasized the importance of broadening participation and building partnerships to ensure a smooth transition between the Turkish and Ethiopian COP presidencies. Ethiopia secured the right to host COP32 following negotiations at COP30 in Belém, Brazil, last year, defeating Nigeria's competing bid. The summit is scheduled to take place in Addis Abeba in November 2027. However, Ethiopia's preparations unfold against persistent disagreements over climate financing, particularly between developed and developing countries. At COP31, the question of adaptation financing remains a major concern for African countries, which have repeatedly called for more predictable and accessible funding to address climate-related vulnerabilities. ethiopia.summary: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has called on major greenhouse gas emitters to enhance their emissions reductions and expedite climate financing as Ethiopia prepares to host the 32nd United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP32) in November 2027. During COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, Abiy emphasized the need for countries with significant historical emissions to take the lead in cutting emissions, highlighting the diversion of resources from essential development areas like education and healthcare due to climate-related damages. His diplomatic outreach included meetings with leaders from Somalia, Barbados, Finland, Norway, Qatar, Iraq, and Botswana, focusing on bilateral cooperation and climate diplomacy. Abiy also discussed Ethiopia's initiatives, such as restrictions on petrol and diesel vehicle imports, aimed at transitioning to electric mobility. As Ethiopia gears up for COP32, the challenge remains to secure concrete commitments on climate financing and adaptation, particularly for vulnerable nations facing severe climate impacts.

Advertisement The Ghana Football Association and the Black Stars wish to express our profound appreciation to the fans in Takoradi for the love, energy and passion they showed the team during Thursday’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Somalia at the Sekondi Sports Stadium. From the first whistle to the last, the buoyant crowd cheered the team on, creating an incredible atmosphere that pushed the players to a scintillating 2-0 victory — Ghana’s first win of the qualifying campaign. The love shown by the people of Takoradi, from the streets to the stands, did not go unnoticed. It was felt by every player, every member of the technical team, and every official. It was a true home advantage. The Black Stars say a big thank you to Takoradi for standing behind the team in a must-win game and for showing what Ghanaian football passion is all about. The job, however, is not done yet. The team will be back in action on Monday, November 16, 2026, for the return fixture against Somalia, and we call on all our fans in Takoradi and beyond to show up again — in your numbers, in your colours, with the same love, energy and passion. Let’s fill the stadium again. Let’s push the Black Stars to another victory. Thank you, Takoradi. See you on Monday. somalia.summary: The Ghana Football Association (GFA) and the Black Stars expressed their heartfelt gratitude to the fans in Takoradi for their unwavering support during the recent Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Somalia. The match, held at Sekondi Sports Stadium, saw the Black Stars secure a 2-0 victory, marking their first win in the qualifying campaign. The enthusiastic crowd created an electrifying atmosphere that motivated the players throughout the game. The GFA acknowledged the significant impact of the fans' passion and energy, emphasizing that it felt like a true home advantage. As the team prepares for the return fixture against Somalia on November 16, 2026, they are calling on fans to replicate their support, urging them to fill the stadium once again with the same fervor. The Black Stars aim to build on their recent success and are hopeful for another victory with the fans' backing.

Follow CTP on X , LinkedIn , and BlueSky . Contributors: Ziv Zellars Key Takeaways: Somalia. The Somali Supreme Court invalidated President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s March 2026 term extension and mandated federal elections within 90 days, intensifying the Federal Government of Somalia’s (FGS’s) political standoff with the national opposition amid uprisings in multiple federal member states. The FGS’s political disputes threaten to create security gaps for al Shabaab to exploit amid international counterterrorism troop withdrawals. Sudan. The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) has advanced along the main east–west highway in central Sudan, as the military attempts to expel the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) from the North and South Kordofan states and advance into RSF-controlled western Sudan. The RSF advanced on a secondary front in southeastern Sudan's Blue Nile state, however, which could distract the SAF from the main front lines in central Sudan. Figure 1. Africa File, November 12, 2026 Source: Emily Bjerke. Assessments: Somalia Author: Michael DeAngelo with Ziv Zellars The Somali Supreme Court invalidated President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s March 2026 term extension and mandated federal elections within 90 days, intensifying the political standoff between the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS) and national opposition. The court ruled on November 5 that the FGS had unlawfully extended Mohamud’s term when it approved a new constitution in March 2026. [1] The new constitution delayed federal elections by one year and extended his term by exactly one year, until May 15, 2027. [2] The court also called on the FGS and national opposition to reach a consensus on an election plan within 30 days and hold federal elections within 90 days. [3] The Somali Supreme Court’s ruling supports the national opposition’s resistance to the term extension and delayed elections. The leading national opposition coalition, the Somali Future Council (SFC), endorsed the court’s ruling on November 7. [4] A main SFC leader, former Somali President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed, had initially filed the motion challenging the new constitution with the Somali Supreme Court. [5] The SFC has been locked in political standoff with the FGS since the approval of the new constitution, which the SFC denounced as an illegitimate power grab. The opposition has mobilized against the FGS by holding press conferences, organizing public demonstrations, and threatening to hold parallel elections. [6] The FGS has responded by restricting SFC leaders’ movements and cracking down on public demonstrations. [7] The standoff has continued since clashes in early June between forces loyal to the two sides in Mogadishu, the Somali capital, despite international mediation efforts. [8] The FGS has challenged the Somali Supreme Court’s authority since the ruling and reaffirmed its own electoral agenda, although the FGS has also moderated its public stance. The FGS had ordered the dismissal of Somali Supreme Court Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed before the ruling, but the court rejected the order. [9] The Somali attorney general and defense minister rejected the ruling shortly after the court announced it. [10] Federal forces then reportedly took over the court, and the FGS removed Yusuf from office and installed a new chief justice on November 7, which the SFC denounced. [11] The FGS and SFC reportedly agreed to talks from November 14 to 18 that the United States, Turkey, the United Kingdom, and the European Union will mediate, however. [12] FGS security officials and SFC leaders held preliminary talks on November 10. [13] The Somali information minister stated after that the FGS still plans to hold direct elections but is open to technical compromises, which it had not previously stated. [14] The FGS is also facing armed uprisings in the Hirshabelle and South West states over its moves to install pro-FGS governments that are further straining federal authority and political bandwidth. The influential Hawadle clan launched a rebellion in Hirshabelle’s Hiiraan region in late October 2026 due to the FGS favoring a member from a different clan for the state presidency, which Hawadle members have argued violated traditional power-sharing agreements. [15] Hawadle militiamen seized key government facilities in Beledweyne, the Hiiraan regional capital, on October 30. [16] A key Hawadle leader then called on the clan to mobilize against the FGS on November 6, causing groups of Hawadle from the federal security forces to defect. [17] Former Somali intelligence head Abdullahi Mohamed Ali Sanbalolshe, who is a leader of the uprising, stated that the clan plans to form a new Hiiraan regional government. [18] Mohamud offered on November 8 to move the Hirshabelle state capital to Hiiraan in an effort to ease tensions, but Sanbalolshe rejected the offer. [19] South West state opposition forces have increasingly threatened the FGS-backed South West state government’s control of the state in late 2026. The opposition forces have sought to overthrow the South West state government since the FGS deposed then-South West state president Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed (Laftagareen) in March and set up a pro-FGS administration. [20] Opposition forces loyal to Laftagareen launched a rebellion in May 2026, recently captured three district capitals in early and mid-October, and have attacked Baidoa—the de facto South West state capital—at least nine times, most recently on November 2. [21] Figure 2. South West Opposition Offensive Against Federally Backed State Government Source: Michael DeAngelo; Ziv Zellars. The FGS’s political disputes threaten to create security gaps for al Shabaab to exploit amid international counterterrorism troop withdrawals. Uganda announced on November 2 that it had begun withdrawing its approximately 2,000 troops stationed in Somalia on a bilateral basis and would complete the process quickly. [22] Ugandan forces were responsible for securing key infrastructure and supply lines into Mogadishu. [23] The Associated Press reported that African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM) forces—the FGS’s most significant external supporter on-the-ground—will take over Ugandan bases, although Uganda and the other AUSSOM member countries also plan to completely withdraw their AUSSOM forces by the end of 2027. [24] The United States separately redeployed forces stationed at the Baledogle Air Base, which is 65 miles northwest of Mogadishu, to “other parts of Somalia” in late October. [25] The United States reportedly used the base to train Somali troops and conduct airstrikes. [26] Al Shabaab has already taken advantage of the FGS’s disputes in Hirshabelle and South West. Al Shabaab announced a peace agreement with Hawadle factions, who play a fundamental role in enabling federally backed counterterrorism operations in central Somalia, in Hiiraan in early October. [27] Al Shabaab has separately increased its monthly attacks in South West by approximately 35 percent since March. [28] The Critical Threats Project (CTP) also previously assessed that South West opposition forces are almost certainly deconflicting and possibly coordinating with al Shabaab. [29] CTP has repeatedly assessed since late 2025 that al Shabaab may also exploit the national political crisis to target sensitive areas in and around Mogadishu. [30] Figure 3. Al Shabaab Increases Activity Following Federal Takeover in South West State, 2026 Source: Michael DeAngelo; Ziv Zellars; Armed Conflict Location & Event Data. Sudan Author: Michael DeAngelo with Liam Karr and Ziv Zellars The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) has advanced along the main east–west highway in central Sudan, as the military attempts to expel the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) from the North and South Kordofan states and advance into RSF-controlled western Sudan. The SAF and allied militias advanced west from al Ayara to capture um Sumeima—approximately 40 miles west of el Obeid, the SAF's central Sudan headquarters and the North Kordofan state capital—on November 5. [31] A spokesperson from the allied Joint Forces militia claimed that the advancing forces had destroyed or captured dozens of RSF combat vehicles. [32] The paramilitary RSF and SAF have traded control of um Sumeima several times since 2025, and the RSF had used the town as a staging ground for attacks on el Obeid throughout 2026. [33] The recapture of the town gives the SAF control of the entire main east–west highway in North Kordofan and gives the SAF positions along the highway on the West Kordofan state border. The SAF also continued making gains on an alternative axis through the North Kordofan desert and advanced into West Kordofan for the first time since late 2025. The military captured um Marahik, which is 140 miles northwest of el Obeid, on November 3. [34] The SAF then reportedly took Iyal Bakhit, which is approximately 115 miles northwest of el Obeid, and several nearby villages on November 7. [35] The Critical Threats Project previously assessed that the SAF’s gains in rural North Kordofan were setting conditions to support the SAF’s primary effort to advance west along Sudan’s main east–west highway toward the RSF-controlled Darfur region. [36] SAF gains to the north create opportunities for the SAF to flank RSF positions on the highway in West Kordofan towns such as al Khawai, which is approximately 70 miles west of el Obeid, as the rural villages link to the highway via secondary roads. [37] Figure 4. Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) Offensive in Central Sudan Note: RSF stands for Rapid Support Forces. Source: Michael DeAngelo; Liam Karr. The SAF has also attempted to advance south of el Obeid to capture an RSF salient along the main north–south highway linking North and South Kordofan with secondary highways leading to West Kordofan. The SAF briefly seized Kazgil—approximately 30 miles south of el Obeid—on November 5, although the RSF reportedly retook the town. [38] Kazgil is a key frontline position in an RSF salient along the highway between SAF-controlled el Obeid and Dilling, which is 100 miles to the south. The salient includes the key crossroads South Kordofan town of al Dabibat, which links to secondary highways that run into West Kordofan and Darfur. The RSF advanced on a secondary front in southeastern Sudan's Blue Nile state, however, which could distract the SAF from the main front lines in central Sudan. The paramilitary group captured Sali, which is 80 miles south of Ad Damazin, the Blue Nile state capital, on November 3. [39] The SAF had used Sali as a key defensive position on Blue Nile’s main north–south highway, which leads toward vital agricultural areas and population centers in the Nile River Valley. [40] The RSF then reportedly took al Keili, which is another SAF base approximately 10 miles east of Sali, on November 4. [41] The RSF also reportedly advanced on an alternative axis via secondary roads that connect to the main highway, recapturing Bakori—approximately 80 miles southeast of Ad Damazin—on November 5. [42] Figure 5. Rapid Support Forces (RSF) Offensive in Blue Nile State Note: SAF stands for Sudanese Armed Forces. Source: Michael DeAngelo; Liam Karr. The RSF’s gains in Blue Nile could distract the SAF from its central Sudan offensive, as past RSF advances have diverted SAF resources to the secondary front. The SAF sent special forces units and other reinforcements to Blue Nile in late August to counter an RSF offensive. [43] The military replaced its Blue Nile commander on November 8. somalia.summary: The Somali Supreme Court has overruled President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term extension, mandating federal elections within 90 days. This ruling intensifies the political standoff between the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS) and the national opposition, particularly the Somali Future Council (SFC), which has mobilized against the FGS since the controversial constitution was approved in March 2026. The FGS has faced armed uprisings in various states, notably from the influential Hawadle clan in Hirshabelle, which has seized key facilities and rejected offers to ease tensions. Meanwhile, the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) have made significant advances along the central highway, attempting to expel the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) from North and South Kordofan. The SAF's recent gains could facilitate further operations into RSF-controlled areas, while the ongoing conflict in Sudan continues to evolve with both sides vying for strategic control. The political instability in Somalia poses risks for security, particularly with al Shabaab potentially exploiting the situation. (157 words)

somalia.content: UN Experts Condemn Somalia's Chief Justice Dismissal as Unlawful, Call for His Restoration - Somali News today Live Home Politics Security Elections More News Premium Economy & Business Education Entertainment & Lifestyle Environment & Climate Health International Relations Technology & Innovation Sports News By Region Nationwide Benadir Galmudug Hirshabelle Jubaland Puntland South West State Somaliland North Eastern State Resources Infographics Downloads Videos FAQ About Somalia Generic selectors Exact matches only Search in title Search in content Post Type Selectors Home Politics Security Elections More News Premium Economy & Business Education Entertainment & Lifestyle Environment & Climate Health International Relations Technology & Innovation Sports News By Region Nationwide Benadir Galmudug Hirshabelle Jubaland Puntland South West State Somaliland North Eastern State Resources Infographics Downloads Videos FAQ About Somalia Generic selectors Exact matches only Search in title Search in content Post Type Selectors Generic selectors Exact matches only Search in title Search in content Post Type Selectors Politics Nationwide UN Experts Condemn Somalia’s Chief Justice Dismissal as Unlawful, Call for His Restoration November 13, 2026 5 min read GENEVA , Two United Nations human rights experts have condemned the Somali government’s dismissal of Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed and the swearing-in of his replacement as unlawful violations of judicial independence, calling for the Chief Justice to be restored to office and for security forces to stand down. In a statement issued on November 12, Margaret Satterthwaite, the Special Rapporteur on the independence of judges and lawyers, and Ben Saul, the Special Rapporteur on human rights while countering terrorism, said the unilateral dismissal of the Chief Justice by presidential decree “did not follow constitutional procedures, including approval by Parliament or a proposal from the Judicial Services Commission.” They described the quick replacement of the Chief Justice within days, and without following legal procedures, as an act that “undermines the rule of law.” The statement adds the weight of international law to a crisis that has unfolded rapidly since the dismissal on November 4. According to the UN experts, the removal occurred the night before the Supreme Court was due to rule on the constitutionality of recent measures extending the terms of the President and Parliament. The following day, five judges proceeded with the case and ruled that the extensions were unlawful, that the mandates of both Parliament and the President had expired, and that elections should be held within 90 days, as detailed in the coverage of the ruling . The judges also declared the dismissal of the Chief Justice unconstitutional and said it had sought to obstruct the court’s consideration of the term extensions. The UN statement confirms that the government refused to comply with these orders, instead deploying hundreds of security personnel to the Supreme Court to disrupt and intimidate the court. Seven Supreme Court judges had their personal security protection withdrawn and were banned from travelling. On November 7, a ceremony was held to swear in Ibrahim Idle Suleiman as the purported new Chief Justice, with President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud in attendance, as reported in the coverage of the swearing-in . The Legal Framework The UN experts grounded their condemnation in established principles of judicial independence. “Judges must be free to decide matters without improper influence, pressure, threat or interference,” they said. They may be suspended or removed only for reasons of incapacity or behaviour that renders them unfit to discharge their duties. The safeguards that must govern the selection and appointment of judges are set out in the Principles for Judicial Appointments. They also linked the judicial crisis to Somalia’s security challenges. Concerns have previously been raised, they noted, that “irregular and contested processes of constitutional reform” and “the lack of an independent judiciary” could undermine counter-terrorism and stabilisation efforts “at a time of grave peril from Al Shabaab.” “We condemn the attempted intimidation of judges and serious threats to their security – their personal protection must be urgently reinstated,” the experts said. “We call on security forces to stand down.” The statement is the most direct international legal intervention in the crisis since it began. It will be cited by the opposition, which has argued that the government’s actions are unconstitutional, and by the judges themselves, who have continued to assert their legitimacy despite the security deployment. The government has not yet responded. Its Attorney General has previously said the Supreme Court’s ruling “has no legal effect,” as reported in the coverage of the Attorney General’s position . Critical Note The UN experts’ statement is not a diplomatic expression of concern. It is a legal finding. It says, in plain terms, that the dismissal of the Chief Justice was unlawful, that the swearing-in of his replacement was illegitimate, and that the deployment of security forces to the Supreme Court was an attempt to intimidate the judiciary. The government’s position, that the court’s ruling has no legal effect, is now directly contradicted by two UN Special Rapporteurs whose mandates cover precisely these issues. The statement also makes a connection that the government would prefer to avoid. It suggests that undermining the judiciary is itself a threat to Somalia’s security, not a way to preserve it. The government has justified its actions by citing the need for stability. The UN experts are saying that the rule of law is not an obstacle to stability. It is a condition of it. Whether the statement changes anything on the ground is another question. The government controls the security forces, and it has shown no sign of reversing course. The judges are still banned from travelling, their protection is still withdrawn, and Suleiman is still sitting in the Chief Justice’s chair. A statement from Geneva does not enforce itself. But it does establish a record. It tells the government that its actions are being watched, and it gives the opposition a legal argument that it can carry to the Security Council and the African Union. The crisis is not resolved. It is now a documented violation of international law. somalia.summary: United Nations human rights experts have condemned the Somali government's dismissal of Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed as unlawful, calling for his reinstatement. In a statement released on November 12, experts Margaret Satterthwaite and Ben Saul criticized the unilateral removal by presidential decree, which bypassed constitutional procedures, including parliamentary approval. They highlighted that this dismissal occurred just before the Supreme Court was set to rule on the legality of recent presidential and parliamentary term extensions. The court subsequently declared these extensions unlawful and deemed the Chief Justice's removal unconstitutional. The UN experts emphasized that the government's actions undermine judicial independence and the rule of law, which are essential for stability in Somalia, especially amid ongoing security challenges from Al Shabaab. They also condemned the intimidation of judges and the deployment of security forces to disrupt court proceedings. The government's response has been dismissive, claiming the Supreme Court's ruling lacks legal effect, further complicating the ongoing constitutional crisis.

These are the Ghanaian team's first points in Group C after defeats in the opening two matches against Côte d'Ivoire and Gambia, BBC Sport reports . Missed penalty and two goals The hosts could have taken the lead as early as the 14th minute: Alidu Seidu was brought down in the penalty area, but Somalia goalkeeper Ibrahim Hussein saved Jordan Ayew's penalty. The scoring was opened in first-half stoppage time. Following a corner by Mohammed Kudus, Mohammed Salisu headed the ball across goal, and Jonas Adjetey scored from six yards. Shortly after the hour mark, Felix Afena-Gyan doubled Ghana's advantage: his shot from inside the penalty area went under Hussein and crossed the goal line. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . Group standings After this victory, the four-time African champions are three points behind Côte d'Ivoire and Gambia. These teams were due to play in Bouaké on the same day. Before the November matches, Ghana national team coach Carlos Queiroz left his post by mutual agreement. Ghana women's national team coach Kim Björkegren took temporary charge of the team for the match against Somalia. In another qualifying match, DR Congo defeated Sierra Leone 3-1. Newcastle United forward Yoane Wissa scored the first goal, while the Congolese, with nine points, moved top of Group E. somalia.summary: Ghana's national football team secured a 2-0 victory over Somalia in Sekondi-Takoradi during the qualification round for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON). This win marked Ghana's first points in Group C after suffering defeats in their initial matches against Côte d'Ivoire and Gambia. The match saw a missed penalty in the 14th minute when Jordan Ayew's shot was saved by Somalia's goalkeeper, Ibrahim Hussein. However, Ghana opened the scoring in first-half stoppage time with Jonas Adjetey netting a goal following a corner from Mohammed Kudus. Felix Afena-Gyan extended the lead shortly after the hour mark with a shot that slipped past Hussein. Following this victory, Ghana trails Côte d'Ivoire and Gambia by three points in the group standings. The match was overseen by Kim Björkegren, the interim coach, after the departure of Carlos Queiroz. In another qualifying match, DR Congo defeated Sierra Leone 3-1.

Ilo-wareedyo xog-ogaal u ah arrintan ayaa sheegay in dalacsiinta ay qayb ka tahay dadaallo ay Villa Somalia ku dooneyso inay ku xakameyso kacdoonka iyo diidmada sii xoogeysanaysa ee ka jirta qaybo ka mid ah bulshada gobolka Hiiraan. Sida ay ilo-wareedyadu sheegeen, qaar ka mid ah dadka lagu daray liiska dalacsiinta ayaa la sheegay in hal mar laga dallacsiiyay darajooyin hoose oo gaarsiisan Korneyl ilaa darajada Jeneraal. Waxaa sidoo kale liiska ku jira shaqsiyaad rayid ah oo aan hore uga diiwaangashanayn ciidamada qalabka sida. Ilo-wareedyadu ma aysan shaacin tirada guud ee dadka la dalacsiiyay, magacyadooda ama hay'adaha ay ka tirsan yihiin. Sidoo kale, lama helin faahfaahin rasmi ah oo ku saabsan shuruudaha lagu saleeyay dalacsiinta iyo habraaca loo maray. Xogaha la helay ayaa tilmaamaya in qaar ka mid ah shaqsiyaadka la dalacsiiyay loo arko inay saameyn ku yeelan karaan xaaladda ka taagan Beledweyne, isla markaana ay gacan ka geysan karaan dejinta kacdoonka iyo abaabulka mucaaradka ee ka dhanka ah maamulka Hirshabelle iyo dowladda federaalka. Hase yeeshee, lama xaqiijin in dadka la dalacsiiyay ay aqbaleen xilalka ama darajooyinka loo magacaabay, ama inay awood u leeyihiin inay beddelaan mowqifka siyaasadeed ee hoggaanka dhaqanka iyo bulshada deegaanka. Dalacsiintan ayaa ku soo beegmaysa xilli uu gobolka Hiiraan ka jiro khilaaf siyaasadeed iyo mid amni oo sii xoogeysanaya, kaddib markii hoggaanka dhaqanka ee beesha Xawaadle, Ugaas Yuusuf Ugaas Xasan Ugaas Khaliif, uu ciidanka iyo bulshada deegaanka ugu baaqay inay isugu yimaadaan magaalada Beledweyne, isagoo ka digay xaaladda ka taagan gobolka. Xiisadda ayaa sidoo kale la xiriirta khilaafka ka dhashay doorashadii maamulka Hirshabelle, gaar ahaan dib-u-doorashadii Madaxweyne Cali Cabdullaahi Xuseen (Guudlaawe), taas oo ay diideen qaar ka mid ah siyaasiyiinta, waxgaradka iyo hoggaanka dhaqanka ee Hiiraan. Dhanka kale, khilaafka siyaasadeed ee dalka ayaa sii xoogeysanaya, iyadoo Maxkamadda Sare ee Soomaaliya ay go'aamisay in muddo-xileedka Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud uu dhammaaday 15-kii May 2026, isla markaana dowladda ku amartay in la gaaro heshiis siyaasadeed oo ku saabsan doorashooyinka. Ilaa hadda, Villa Somalia si rasmi ah ugama aysan hadlin wararka ku saabsan dalacsiinta la sheegay in loo sameeyay xubnaha ka soo jeeda Hiiraan, mana jirto faahfaahin madax-bannaan oo xaqiijinaysa liiska dadka la dalacsiiyay iyo darajooyinka la siiyay. Dalacsiinta la sheegay ayaa imanaysa xilli ay dowladda federaalka wajahayso caqabado la xiriira xiriirka ay la leedahay bulshada Hiiraan, isku-duubnaanta ciidamada iyo khilaafaadka siyaasadeed ee dalka. somalia.summary: Villa Somalia, led by President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, is reportedly promoting military personnel from the Hiiraan region, specifically from the Xawaadle clan, amid rising political and security tensions in Beledweyne. This military promotion is seen as an effort to quell unrest and opposition against the Hirshabelle administration and the federal government. Sources indicate that some individuals have been elevated from lower ranks to positions as high as General, including civilians not previously affiliated with the military. However, the total number of those promoted and their identities remain undisclosed, as does the official process behind these promotions. The situation is further complicated by ongoing political disputes following the recent Hirshabelle elections, which have faced rejection from various local leaders. Additionally, the Somali Supreme Court has ruled that President Mohamud's term ended on May 15, 2026, prompting calls for a political agreement on upcoming elections.

beat Somalia in Sekondi Scintillating Black Stars beat Somalia in Sekondi 2 hours ago Advertisement The Black Stars recorded their first win in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers with a scintillating 2-0 victory over Somalia at the Sekondi Sports Stadium on Thursday. Ghana had to survive an early scare when captain Jordan Ayew missed a rare penalty in the 13th minute, but the team responded in style to dominate proceedings. Jonas Adjetey scored his first international goal for Ghana in the 47th minute, just before the break, to give Ghana a narrow lead heading into half-time. Ghana dominated with Thomas Partey, Caleb Yirenkyi and Abdul Fatawu Issahaku controlling affairs in midfield. Mohammed Kudus was a delight to watch as he took charge of the game with some blistering displays and phenomenal pace, being a thorn in the flesh of the Somali defence. Turkey-based forward Felix Afena-Gyan added the second goal in the 62nd minute after a combination play between Thomas Partey, Jordan Ayew and Mohammed Kudus, before a sensational through pass set up Afena-Gyan to slam home. The Black Stars then took a commanding lead in front of a buoyant crowd that cheered the team from start to finish. Prince Adu Kwabena came on for Afena-Gyan two minutes later as Ghana continued to push for more goals. Kim Lars Bjorkegren introduced Daniel Kofi Kyereh for his first major appearance since 2022 as he came on for captain Jordan Ayew. Ibrahim Sulemana also made an entry for Alidu Seidu inside 75 minutes. In search of more goals to consolidate the win, Brandon Thomas-Asante made an entry for Abdul Fatawu Issahaku, as Ibrahim Rash was brought on for Caleb Yirenkyi with four minutes remaining. Somalia had one decent shot on target in the 88th minute but it was not enough to trouble Benjamin Asare, who had a decent afternoon for Ghana. The Black Stars kept pressing for a third, but the Somalis kept their defence intact and held on until the blast of the whistle as Ghana won 2-0. The win gives Ghana their first three points of the qualifying campaign after defeats to Cote D’Ivoire and The Gambia in their opening two games. Ghana will play against Somalia in the 4th game of the campaign a the Sekondi Stadium on Monday, November 16, 2026. Despite an early setback when captain Jordan Ayew missed a penalty, Ghana quickly regained control. Jonas Adjetey netted his first international goal just after halftime, giving Ghana a 1-0 lead. The team showcased strong midfield dominance, particularly through players like Thomas Partey and Mohammed Kudus, who consistently troubled the Somali defense. Felix Afena-Gyan extended the lead to 2-0 in the 62nd minute following a well-coordinated play. Although Somalia managed a late shot on target, it posed no threat to Ghana's goalkeeper, Benjamin Asare. This victory marks Ghana's first points in the qualifying campaign after previous losses to Cote D’Ivoire and The Gambia. The Black Stars are set to face Somalia again on November 16, 2026, in their next qualifying match. (159 words)

By David Bolarinwa November 12, 2026 8:58 PM GMT+1 Ghana recorded their first victory in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign with a 2-0 win over Somalia at the Essipong Sports Stadium on Thursday. Defender Jonas Adjetey opened the scoring in first-half stoppage time before substitute Felix Afena-Gyan doubled the Black Stars’ lead in the 62nd minute. The victory lifted Ghana off the bottom of Group C and eased some of the pressure on interim coach Kim Lars Björkegren, while Somalia remain without a point after three matches. Ghana dominated the opening half but struggled to break down Somalia’s defensive formation. Captain Jordan Ayew missed a 14th-minute penalty, with goalkeeper Ibrahim Ahmed saving his effort. Read Also: Ghana Welcome Back Kudus, Ayew For Crucial AFCON Qualifier ADVERTISEMENT The hosts eventually found the breakthrough in the 45th minute, with Adjetey converting a delivery from Mohammed Salisu to give Ghana a 1-0 lead at the interval. Read Also Ghana Welcome Back Kudus, Ayew For Crucial AFCON Qualifier Ghana, UK Review Ties Ahead Of Mahama’s Official Visit FBI Arrests 130+ in Ghana Over Global Scam Network Afena-Gyan extended the advantage in the 62nd minute, giving the Black Stars a comfortable cushion and leaving Somalia with a difficult task in their attempt to get back into the game. The two sides will meet again on Monday, November 16, at the same venue, with the return fixture officially designated as Somalia’s home game. The match is being staged in Ghana because Somalia does not have a Confederation of African Football-approved stadium for international fixtures. Ghana began their qualifying campaign with defeats to Côte d’Ivoire and The Gambia, results that contributed to the departure of former coach Carlos Queiroz. ADVERTISEMENT The return of key players, including Mohammed Kudus, Thomas Partey and Jordan Ayew, was expected to strengthen the team as Björkegren took charge. Thursday’s result gives Ghana an opportunity to build momentum ahead of Monday’s return fixture, while Somalia will seek a response after another defeat in the qualifying campaign. Ahmed and her business partner want to convert 5,000 petrol tuk tuks to electric alternatives Caroline O'Doherty Thu Nov 12 2026 - 19:43 • 3 MIN READ Hassan Mumin and Fadumo Ahmed of Somali social enterprise eBajaaj at Cop31 in Antalya, Turkey. Photograph: Caroline O'Doherty T here are 75,000 tuk tuks in Mogadishu, spewing choking petrol fumes into the Somali capital’s air, filling its streets with unrelenting noise and driving up carbon emissions. Only four women are licensed to drive them and one, Fadumo Ahmed, is planning a revolution. Ahmed (32) and her business partner, Hassan Mumin (31), have set up eBajaaj, a social enterprise that aims to electrify the tuk tuk fleet. They have 20 converted tuk tuks on the streets, the three-wheeled passenger vehicles stripped of their petrol motors to carry battery packs instead. READ MORE US official discloses nearly $12,000 holiday paid for by Stripe’s Patrick Collison Zelenskiy says Europe to be included in Ukraine peace talks as he meets US envoys in Dublin Ann Dunne, daughter of Dunnes Stores founder, dies Conor Murray: Why Mack Hansen could be key to Ireland’s 2027 World Cup ambitions Their goal is to convert 5,000 – to start with anyway. “I’m an entrepreneur but also a climate activist,” Ahmed says. Entrepreneurs need investors and that’s why Ahmed is at Cop31 . She’s trying to get the attention of the many banks, investment houses and financial advisers that circle the corridors, often talking the talk about investing in the green transition but slow to put their money into transformative projects. “We approached local banks but it’s a new technology in a fragile market,” Mumin says. “The risk is too high for them.” Working on converting a petrol-powered tuk tuk to an electric vehicle at Somali social enterprise eBajaaj. So here’s their pitch. A tuk tuk driver pays $15 (€13.41) a day to fuel his vehicle and $20 twice a month for an oil change. “He is going home with $2-3 a day,” says Ahmed. “It’s not enough. People are hungry.” The $2,500 cost of buying and installing the battery conversion kit for each tuk tuk will be paid by eBajaaj. It also builds charging depots – simple roadside shelters with solar panels on the roof where drivers can quickly swap their battery for a fully charged replacement stored in a secure locker while empty batteries are charged in just two hours. The tuk tuk owners pay a subscription of $4 a day to cover the price of charging and a contribution towards the cost of the conversion. Eventually, those contributions build up and, with savings in running costs, they can pay the price of the conversion kit over time. “They don’t know much about climate or emissions. They’re concerned about savings and what they can do for their families and that I believe is the biggest benefit from this.” [ Caroline O'Doherty at Cop31: Tuvaluan of Irish ancestry fights climate change and despair Opens in new window ] Getting ready for the road at the eBajaaj electric tuk tuk charging depot in Mogadishu. There are other benefits less obvious to an outsider. “The tuk tuks are automatic so it’s easier for women to drive,” says Ahmed. “Also, Somalia has had civil war and many people have lost their arms, their hands, but this is going to be easy for them to drive too.” A surprising side effect is an easing of the traffic jams at Mogadishu’s many security checkpoints. Tuk tuks are regularly checked for weapons and explosives, a task that involves getting the driver out of his seat and the seat lifted. The electric tuk tuks have clear space under the seats so checks are quickly completed. Ahmed spends a lot of time talking to drivers in person and online, countering claims that the batteries don’t last and the electric tuk tuks can’t be driven in Mogadishu’s sometimes waterlogged streets. For the record, the batteries last 120km and are waterproof, and Ahmed says she wants to lose the petrol companies millions of dollars. She and Mumin have been as brave in their personal lives as they are bold in their entrepreneurial endeavours, Ahmed having moved her family and children back to Somalia from Sweden and Mumin from California. “We want to do something good for our country and for climate,” Ahmed says. “When we talk to people, they say wow, that’s inspiring. somalia.summary: Fadumo Ahmed, a 32-year-old entrepreneur from Somalia, is making strides in environmental sustainability by aiming to convert 5,000 petrol tuk tuks in Mogadishu to electric alternatives through her social enterprise, eBajaaj. Currently, the city has 75,000 petrol tuk tuks, contributing to severe air pollution and high carbon emissions. Ahmed and her partner, Hassan Mumin, have already converted 20 tuk tuks and are seeking investment at Cop31 to expand their project. The initiative not only addresses environmental concerns but also offers economic benefits to drivers, who currently spend significant amounts on fuel and maintenance. By switching to electric, drivers can save money and improve their livelihoods. The project also facilitates easier driving for women and those with disabilities, while speeding up security checks at checkpoints. Ahmed emphasizes the need for investment to realize their vision of a cleaner, more sustainable future for Somalia.

football.summary: أعلنت لجنة الاستئناف بالاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم قرارًا مفاجئًا بشأن لقب الدوري السوداني، حيث ألغت قرارها السابق الذي منح اللقب لنادي المريخ، وأعادت اللقب لنادي الهلال. جاء هذا القرار بعد قبول طلب المراجعة المقدم من الهلال، الذي أكد استحقاقه للقب بعد فوزه على المريخ في المباراة الأخيرة من الموسم الماضي. وأوضحت اللجنة أنها عقدت اجتماعين في 9 و10 نوفمبر، حيث استندت إلى تقرير الحكم في المباراة. وأصدر نادي الهلال بيانًا رسميًا يعلن فيه استرداده للقب، مؤكدًا مكانته كأكثر الأندية تتويجًا بالبطولات في السودان. يذكر أن الموسم الماضي شهد جدلًا كبيرًا حول قانونية مشاركة بعض لاعبي الهلال، مما أدى إلى منح اللقب للمريخ بعد استئناف. هذا القرار يعيد الأمور إلى نصابها ويؤكد تفوق الهلال في الساحة الرياضية السودانية.

football.title: باللجوء للمحكمة الرياضية.. أزمة سحب لقب الدوري السوداني من المريخ تتصاعد - متن نيوز
football.content: زمة سحب لقب الدوري السوداني من المريخ تتصاعد الجمعة 13 نوفمبر 2026 facebook twitter youtube instagram whatsapp rss feed احدث الاخبار تلفزيون متن الرياضة السياسة الاقتصاد تقارير وتحقيقات الدراسات والابحاث باللجوء للمحكمة الرياضية.. أزمة سحب لقب الدوري السوداني من المريخ تتصاعد المريخ السوداني الأربعاء 11/نوفمبر/2026 - 06:03 م 11/11/2026 6:03:24 PM الرياضة شارك طباعة أكد نادي المريخ السوداني، على رفضه القاطع لقرار لجنة الاستئناف المتعلق بشأن لقب الدوري للموسم الماضي، بعد قبول اللجنة لطلب الفحص من الهلال. وأعلن نادي الهلال مساء أمس الثلاثاء، حصوله على لقب الدوري السوداني الموسم الماضي، بقرار رسمي صادر من قبل لجنة الاستئناف في الاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم. وشدد المريخ السوداني في بيانه الرسمي الذي أصدره عبر صفحاته الرسمية، على رفضه القاطع لقرار لجنة الاستئنافات، مؤكدًا على تصعيد القضية إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية "كاس". وجاء بيان المريخ السوداني كالتالي: "يعلن نادي المريخ الرياضي رفضه القاطع لقرار لجنة الاستئنافات المشكلة حديثًا، والقاضي بقبول طلب الفحص المقدم من النادي الآخر، ونقض القرار السابق الذي قضى بأحقية المريخ في لقب بطولة الدوري الممتاز، وبذلك يؤكد تمسكه بكافة حقوقه ومكتسباته، ورفضه لأي إجراءات تنتقص منها". وواصل في بيانه الرسمي: "ويثير القرار استغراب المجلس، لا سيما أن لجنة الاستئنافات السابقة لم تكتفِ بإصدار قرارها لصالح المريخ، بل أشادت في حيثياته بالاستئناف الذي تقدم به النادي، وأثبتت ذلك صراحة في مضابطها، وهو الأمر الذي قاد الاتحاد السوداني إلى إجراء تعديلات على لائحة أوضاع اللاعبين استنادًا إلى ما انتهت إليه اللجنة للقضية، الأمر الذي يجعل العدول عن ذلك القرار موضع تساؤل قانوني". وأردف في البيان الرسمي: "وتزداد علامات الاستفهام حول القرار الأخير، في ظل تلقي النادي إخطارًا رسميًا من الاتحاد يفيد بانتقال القضية إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية (CAS)، بناءً على الشكوى المقدمة من النادي الآخر بالرقم A/12688. وهو ما يطرح تساؤلات جوهرية حول الأساس القانوني والإجرائي لإعادة النظر في القضية أمام لجنة الاستئنافات، بعد إخطار الأطراف بانتقال النزاع إلى المحكمة الدولية". واستكمل المريخ في بيانه: "وبناءً على كل ذلك وعلى ضوء القرار الأخير حسم مجلس إدارة نادي المريخ أمره وقرر تصعيد القضية إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية (CAS)، والمضي في كافة الإجراءات القانونية اللازمة، مستندًا إلى خبرات النادي وتجاربه السابقة أمام المحكمة، ومستعينًا بالكفاءات القانونية المتخصصة، دفاعًا عن حقه في البطولة حتى صدور القرار النهائي". وأردف النادي السوداني في بيانه: "وفي هذا الصدد يوجه المجلس وجماهير النادي ورموزه ونجومه وإعلامه وكافة قطاعاته رسالة واضحة إلى الاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم، بأن المريخ نادٍ جماهيري وقيادي، له تاريخه ومكانته وقاعدته الممتدة داخل السودان وخارجه، لذلك لن يقبل المساس بحقوقه أو الانتقاص من مقدراته". واستكمل: "وعلى الاتحاد الالتزام بمسؤولياته في إدارة المنافسة بعدالة وأخلاق وحياد، إضافة إلى تطبيق اللوائح دون تمييز أو انتقائية، ونعيد التأكيد بأقوى العبارات أن المريخ لن يقف مكتوف الأيدي أمام أي إجراءات تمس حقوقه، ولن يقبل فرض الأمر الواقع عليه أو العبث بمكتسباته، وسيواجه ذلك بكل الوسائل القانونية والمؤسسية المتاحة". واختتم النادي بيانه: "وإلى جماهير المريخ الوفية، يؤكد المجلس أن حقوق النادي ليست محل مساومة أو تفريط، وأنه ماضٍ في طريق القانون حتى النهاية، وأنتم من خلفنا سندًا والعهد بيننا ألا تراجع إطلاقًا". وقد حسم الدوري السوداني في الموسم الماضي، بشكل مثير للجدل، حيث توج المريخ باللقب رغم فوز الهلال بهدف نظيف في الجولة الأخيرة من البطولة، وجاء ذلك بعد قبول استئناف المريخ ضد قرار لجنة المسابقات بشأن قانونية مشاركة عدد من لاعبي الهلال خلال مباراة القمة بين الفريقين. شارك المريخ السوداني الهلال لجنة الاستئناف نادي المريخ الدوري السوداني الأكثر مشاهدة خروج عربة قطار عن القضبان على خط الإسماعيلية السويس دون وقوع إصابات (صور) البورصة المصرية تبدأ تعاملات الخميس بتراجع EGX30 وصعود مؤشري الشركات الصغيرة والمتوسطة السيسي يتابع تطوير مطارات العلمين وسفنكس والعاصمة الجديدة اتصال هاتفي من مرموش للتوأم حسن.. رسالة شكر بعد قرار الإقالة المجلس الانتقالي الجنوبي والحوار الوطني.. توافقات سياسية لمواجهة التحديات وترتيب الأولويات منتخب غانا يحقق فوزه الأول في تصفيات أمم إفريقيا 2027 على حساب الصومال تحديد موعد عودة البرازيلي رودريجو إلى مباريات ريال مدريد التميمي يبحث مع النهدي الأوضاع في مديرية العبر والتحديات التي تواجه المواطنين في المنطقة ، هي شبكة إخبارية ناطقة بالعربية تهتم بمستجدات الأحداث العربية والعالمية على مدار الساعة ،وكذلك الأخبار السياسية، والاقتصادية، والثقافية، football.summary: تتصاعد أزمة سحب لقب الدوري السوداني من نادي المريخ بعد قرار لجنة الاستئناف بقبول طلب نادي الهلال للفحص، مما أدى إلى إعلان الهلال فوزه باللقب. نادي المريخ، في بيان رسمي، أعرب عن رفضه القاطع لهذا القرار وأكد عزمه تصعيد القضية إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية (CAS). وأشار المريخ إلى أن القرار الأخير يثير تساؤلات قانونية، خاصة بعد أن أشادت اللجنة السابقة بقرارها لصالحه. كما أكد النادي أنه لن يقبل أي إجراءات تمس حقوقه، مشددًا على أهمية إدارة المنافسة بعدالة وحياد. المريخ يعتزم اتخاذ كافة الإجراءات القانونية اللازمة للدفاع عن حقه في البطولة، مع التأكيد على دعم جماهيره. الدوري السوداني شهد جدلًا كبيرًا حول لقبه، حيث توج المريخ رغم فوز الهلال في الجولة الأخيرة، بعد قبول استئناف المريخ بشأن قانونية مشاركة بعض لاعبي الهلال.

football.title: المريخ السوداني يعلن التصعيد إلى المحكمة الرياضية بعد سحب لقب الدوري - Masrawy
football.content: المريخ السوداني يصعّد أزمة لقب الدوري إلى المحكمة الرياضية الرئيسية رياضة رياضة عالمية المريخ السوداني يعلن التصعيد إلى المحكمة الرياضية بعد سحب لقب الدوري 12:48 م الأربعاء 11 نوفمبر 2026 فريق المريخ السوداني أعلن نادي المريخ السوداني رفضه القاطع لقرار لجنة الاستئنافات بالاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم، بشأن سحب لقب الدوري الممتاز للموسم الماضي ومنحه لمنافسه الهلال، مؤكدًا عزمه تصعيد القضية إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية «كاس» (CAS). إعلان وكانت لجنة الاستئنافات قد أصدرت قرارًا بقبول طلب الفحص المقدم من نادي الهلال، ونقض القرار السابق الذي منح المريخ أحقية التتويج بلقب الدوري، ليعلن الهلال مساء أمس الثلاثاء حصوله رسميًا على البطولة. وتعود تفاصيل الأزمة إلى الجولة الأخيرة من منافسات الدوري السوداني الموسم الماضي، عندما حقق الهلال الفوز على المريخ بهدف دون مقابل، إلا أن الأخير تُوّج باللقب بعد قبول استئنافه ضد قرار لجنة المسابقات بشأن قانونية مشاركة عدد من لاعبي الهلال في مباراة القمة بين الفريقين. المريخ يتمسك بالتصعيد إلى المحكمة الرياضية وأكد مجلس إدارة المريخ، في بيان رسمي نشره عبر منصاته، رفضه قرار لجنة الاستئنافات، مشددًا على تمسكه بكافة حقوقه ومكتسباته، واعتباره القرار الأخير محل تساؤلات قانونية وإجرائية. وأشار النادي إلى أن لجنة الاستئنافات السابقة سبق أن أصدرت قرارًا لصالحه، بل أشادت في حيثياتها بالاستئناف الذي تقدم به، وهو ما دفع الاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم إلى إجراء تعديلات على لائحة أوضاع اللاعبين استنادًا إلى ما انتهت إليه اللجنة في القضية. وأضاف البيان أن علامات الاستفهام تتزايد بشأن القرار الجديد، خاصة بعدما تلقى النادي إخطارًا رسميًا من الاتحاد السوداني يفيد بانتقال النزاع إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية، بناءً على الشكوى المقدمة من الهلال، والمسجلة تحت الرقم A/12688. وأوضح المريخ أن هذا الإجراء يثير تساؤلات بشأن الأساس القانوني لإعادة فتح القضية أمام لجنة الاستئنافات، بعد إخطار الأطراف بانتقال النزاع إلى المحكمة الرياضية الدولية. المريخ: لن نفرط في حقوق النادي وشدد مجلس إدارة النادي على اتخاذ قرار نهائي بتصعيد القضية إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية، والمضي في جميع الإجراءات القانونية اللازمة، بالاستعانة بخبرات قانونية متخصصة، للدفاع عن أحقية الفريق في اللقب حتى صدور الحكم النهائي. كما وجّه المجلس رسالة إلى الاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم، مطالبًا إياه بالالتزام بمسؤولياته في إدارة المسابقات وفق مبادئ العدالة والحياد، وتطبيق اللوائح دون تمييز أو انتقائية. واختتم المريخ بيانه بالتأكيد على أن حقوق النادي ليست محل مساومة أو تفريط، وأنه سيواصل اتخاذ المسارات القانونية والمؤسسية المتاحة للدفاع عن موقفه، مع توجيه رسالة طمأنة إلى جماهيره بأن المجلس متمسك بالقضية حتى النهاية. المريخ السوداني الهلال الدوري السوداني إعلان الأخبار المتعلقة شباب أهلي دبي يعلن جاهزيته لمواجهة الهلال السعودي في دوري أبطال النخبة الهلال يهزم الفتح بثنائية ويستعيد صدارة دوري روشن السعودي إعلان انتصارات مثيرة للهلال والنصر والأهلي والاتحاد في دوري روشن المريخ السوداني يكشف حقيقة تحمله تكاليف ملاعب الزمالك في رواندا الرئيسية أخبار رياضة صور وفيديوهات لايف ستايل فنون سيارات إسلاميات 2026 جميع الحقوق محفوظة لدى
football.summary: أعلن نادي المريخ السوداني تصعيد قضيته بشأن سحب لقب الدوري الممتاز إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية (كاس)، بعد قرار لجنة الاستئنافات بالاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم الذي منح اللقب لمنافسه الهلال. جاء هذا القرار بعد قبول استئناف الهلال الذي طعن في قانونية مشاركة بعض لاعبي المريخ في مباراة القمة. المريخ، الذي كان قد توج باللقب بعد استئناف سابق، أكد في بيان رسمي رفضه القاطع للقرار الجديد، مشددًا على تمسكه بحقوقه ومكتسباته. كما أشار النادي إلى وجود تساؤلات قانونية حول إعادة فتح القضية، خاصة بعد إخطار الأطراف بانتقال النزاع إلى المحكمة الرياضية. وأكد مجلس إدارة المريخ أنه سيواصل اتخاذ الإجراءات القانونية اللازمة للدفاع عن حقه في اللقب، مع التأكيد على عدم التفريط في حقوق النادي.
